jsonld.site_description: Find every civic district that covers a point or address in West Virginia, and who represents you there.
jsonld.app_description: Click any point in West Virginia, or search an address, to see every civic district that contains it, and who represents you there — county, West Virginia Senate, House of Delegates and U.S. House districts, county commissions, magisterial districts, cities, towns and villages, school districts and ZIP codes.
jsonld.keywords: West Virginia district map, what district am I in, West Virginia Senate district, West Virginia House of Delegates district, West Virginia congressional district, West Virginia county commission, West Virginia magisterial district, West Virginia school district lookup

layers.label: U.S. House
layers.rank_note: 2 congressional districts — the largest districts West Virginia carries below the state itself

source.answers: The U.S. House district covering the point, and the representative holding it.

boundary.label: U.S. Census TIGERweb — Legislative, layer 4 (119th Congressional Districts), pre-built for the state and shipped with the app; 2 features for West Virginia, measured 2026-10-29. Layer 0, the 120th Congress's map, draws the same two districts (each district's GEOID and land area equal, every shape the same ground), because West Virginia has not redrawn since its 2021 plan, so nothing changes on 3 January 2027 and the builder refuses to write if the two ever differ. Simplified by Douglas-Peucker at a 5 m interval and refused over an 8 m fidelity ceiling.

source.people: congress-roster.json, rebuilt weekly by CI from the public-domain unitedstates/congress-legislators dataset — including each member's district office and Washington office.

layers.label: West Virginia Senate District
layers.rank_note: 17 Senate districts, two senators each — larger on average than a county, smaller than a congressional district

source.answers: The West Virginia Senate district covering the point, and the two senators who represent it.

boundary.label: West Virginia Legislature — the Senate districts of the 2021 plan as the Legislature publishes them (SENfinal_json.zip on its redistricting page), pre-built for the state and shipped with the app; 17 features, measured 2026-10-29. THE LEGISLATURE'S OWN FILE AND NOT THE CENSUS BUREAU'S: the builder checks it against the state GIS centre's map of the 2021 Senate districts on 2,000 points across the state, and refuses to write under 99.5% agreement. Simplified by Douglas-Peucker at a 5 m interval and refused over an 8 m fidelity ceiling.

source.people: wv-senate-members.json, rebuilt weekly by CI from the West Virginia Senate's own roster page: each senator's name, party, Capitol office (room, telephone) and e-mail address. The page also prints each senator's home county, which is not read. Each district elects two senators, and the card names both.

layers.label: County
layers.rank_note: 55 counties, pre-built from TIGERweb; the instance's offline anchor layer

source.answers: Which county contains the point, who sits on its county commission, and who holds its other elected county offices.

boundary.label: U.S. Census TIGERweb — State_County, layer 1, pre-built for the state and shipped with the app; 55 features, measured 2026-10-29. Simplified by Douglas-Peucker at a 5 m interval and refused over an 8 m fidelity ceiling.

source.people: wv-county-officials.json, rebuilt weekly from the West Virginia Secretary of State's directory of county officials (the newest year that lists all 55 counties; 2025 when this was written): the county commissioners (three in most counties, five in Berkeley and Jefferson), the county clerk, circuit clerk, assessor, sheriff, prosecuting attorney and surveyor, with the telephone and e-mail address the directory prints for that official alone. The board of education is not named yet (gap wv-school-board-members). The card says which year's directory it read.

layers.label: School District
layers.rank_note: 55 county school districts, one for each county, live from TIGERweb (no data/app file)

source.answers: The public school district covering the point.

boundary.label: U.S. Census TIGERweb — School, layer 0 (unified school districts), queried live at runtime; 55 features for West Virginia, one for each county, measured 2026-10-29. The elementary and secondary layers carry nothing for West Virginia.

source.people: NO OFFICEHOLDER YET. Each county's board of education is elected, by the whole county in May of even years, and no list of its members dated after the boards' 1 July 2026 changeover was read in this pass — recorded as gap wv-school-board-members.

layers.label: House of Delegates District
layers.rank_note: 100 single-member delegate districts — smaller on average than a county, larger than a magisterial district

source.answers: The West Virginia House of Delegates district covering the point, and the delegate holding it.

boundary.label: West Virginia Legislature — the House of Delegates districts of the 2021 plan as the Legislature publishes them (HODfinal_json.zip on its redistricting page), pre-built for the state and shipped with the app; 100 features, measured 2026-10-29. THE LEGISLATURE'S OWN FILE AND NOT THE CENSUS BUREAU'S: the Census Bureau's copy puts about 1.4 km2 of Clarksburg in a different district than the plan does, while the state GIS centre's map agrees with the plan; the builder checks the plan against that map on 2,000 points and refuses to write under 99.5% agreement. Simplified by Douglas-Peucker at a 5 m interval and refused over an 8 m fidelity ceiling.

source.people: wv-house-members.json, rebuilt weekly by CI from the House of Delegates' own roster page: each delegate's name, party, Capitol office (room, telephone) and e-mail address.

layers.label: Magisterial District
layers.rank_note: 195 magisterial districts, three to eight in each county, pre-built from the state's own map

source.answers: The magisterial district containing the point and its county. The county commission and board of education draw their members from these districts, so the card says what that means.

boundary.label: WV GIS Technical Center (West Virginia University) — WV_Election_Layers, layer 9 (Magisterial 2026), the statewide map of each county's magisterial districts as the counties sent them to the Secretary of State under W. Va. Code 3-1-5, pre-built and shipped with the app; 195 features in all 55 counties, measured 2026-10-29. THE STATE'S MAP AND NOT THE CENSUS BUREAU'S: the Census files West Virginia's magisterial districts as its county subdivisions, and in many counties its copy predates the counties' current maps. The builder removes 44 drawing slivers under 10 m2 and 70 zero-width spikes from the state's layer before simplifying, and prints what they held on every run. Simplified by Douglas-Peucker at a 5 m interval and refused over an 8 m fidelity ceiling.

source.people: NO OFFICEHOLDER, AND NONE IS MISSING: a magisterial district elects nobody of its own. No two county commissioners may live in the same one (W. Va. Const. art. IX, sec. 10), and no more than two board of education members (W. Va. Code 18-5-1), which is what the card says.

layers.label: ZIP Code
layers.rank_note: 2,017 ZIP Code Tabulation Areas in the state's own bounding box, fetched live by envelope; the layer hides outside West Virginia

source.answers: The ZIP Code Tabulation Area covering the point — the Census Bureau's areal approximation of the USPS delivery routes sharing a ZIP code, not a postal boundary.

boundary.label: U.S. Census TIGERweb — ZIP Code Tabulation Areas, layer 11 of the PUMA/TAD/TAZ/UGA/ZCTA service, queried live at runtime. ZCTAs carry NO STATE FIELD because they cross state lines, so this is the one TIGERweb layer here fetched by a bounding ENVELOPE rather than STATE='54'. 2,017 features in West Virginia's box, which reaches into five neighbouring states, measured 2026-10-29.

source.people: NO OFFICEHOLDER, AND NONE IS MISSING: a ZIP code is a mail-routing convenience, not a unit of government, so nobody is elected from one. The card says what the boundary actually is rather than leaving a reader to assume it means more.
source.applies: West Virginia. The layer is hidden outside the state outline, because outside it the Census's point query answers with a neighbouring state's real ZIP code.

layers.label: City, Town or Village
layers.rank_note: 229 incorporated places, about 5 km2 of land on average, live from TIGERweb

source.answers: The city, town or village containing the point, if any.

boundary.label: U.S. Census TIGERweb — Places_CouSub_ConCity_SubMCD, layer 4 (incorporated places), queried live at runtime; 229 features for West Virginia (78 cities, 144 towns, 6 villages and the Corporation of Ranson), measured 2026-10-29, every one recorded by the Census as an active government.

source.people: NO OFFICEHOLDER YET. West Virginia's cities, towns and villages elect their own officials, and no statewide roster of them was read in this pass; the card names the place and links nothing it has not verified. Recorded as gap wv-municipal-officeholders.
source.applies: West Virginia — statewide. A point outside every city, town and village is unincorporated, which the card states.

layers.label: Police Station
layers.rank_note: nearest police stations by straight-line distance — a point layer, ranked with the other nearest-N layers

source.answers: The three nearest police stations to the point, by straight-line distance, with each one's address.

boundary.label: USGS The National Map — structures layer 53 (Police Stations), queried live at runtime by a bounding envelope through the paged loader. Public domain. Measured 2026-10-29: 862 points in West Virginia's envelope, under the service's 2,000-record cap today, and paged anyway so that stops being a fact anyone has to re-check.

source.people: NO OFFICEHOLDER, AND NONE IS MISSING: a police station is a facility, not an elected district. Nobody is elected from one.
source.applies: West Virginia — plus the border strip its envelope necessarily includes. A BUILDING, NOT A JURISDICTION: which agency answers at a given point is a service-area question this instance has not been researched for, so the card says where the nearest are and never who serves you. Nearest-three is a proximity fact, so for a reader near the state line the nearest one really may be in a neighbouring state, and the card's intro says these are straight-line distances.

anchor_point.note: West Virginia State Capitol, 1900 Kanawha Boulevard East, Charleston, Kanawha County

negative_point.note: Garrett County, Maryland, about 20 km east of the West Virginia line at Preston County — outside West Virginia and outside every other instance in the fleet, and inside permalink_gate so the app answers the click and every shipped layer correctly returns nothing. Measured 2026-10-29: TIGERweb's state and county layers name Maryland and Garrett County here (control: the State Capitol returns West Virginia and Kanawha County), none of the state's shipped boundary files contains it, and no outline in fleet-outlines.json does. A POINT ON A NEIGHBOUR'S LAND WILL HAVE TO MOVE THE DAY THAT NEIGHBOUR GOES LIVE: Kentucky is live already, and Maryland, Pennsylvania, Ohio and Virginia are not, so the change that makes Maryland live moves this point, the way Kentucky's go-live moved Indiana's.
